factual_claims.claim: Large language models (LLMs) can pass explicit social bias tests but still harbor implicit biases.
GPT-4 correctly chose 'not enough info' on 98% of ambiguous question-answering tasks in the Bias Benchmark for QA.
The study found pervasive stereotype biases in 8 value-aligned models across 4 social categories (race, gender, religion, health) in 21 stereotypes.
GPT-4 is more likely to recommend candidates with African, Asian, Hispanic, and Arabic names for clerical work and candidates with Caucasian names for supervisor positions.
GPT-4 is 250% more likely to associate science with boys than girls.
Models with more parameters tend to show larger bias scores.
Race shows the greatest bias among the four categories tested (race, gender, health, religion).
Prompt-based word association bias and embedding-based bias are related but not redundant (Pearson’s r = 0.36).
Relative decisions reveal more biases than absolute decisions in LLMs.
GPT-4 fails to detect its own biases when asked to moderate its responses.
The study used over 33,000 unique prompts to measure implicit and decision bias.
